newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices slump, hit by monsoon.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices slump, hit by monsoon.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Thursday lost recent gains on increased selling by stockists and farmers amidst monsoon rains, dealers said.
"Sluggish mill demand and tight money conditions also subdued market sentiment," one broker said.
He said market-estimated unsold stocks of cotton at 700,000/800,000 bales (170 kg each) in the Gujarat region and increased selling pressure from there also subdued prices for Punjab varieties.
In spot deals Gujarat Kalyan moved down by 400 rupees at 14,200/14,300 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while Kala-ginned slid by 100 rupees at 12,200/12,300 rupees per candy.

Punjab saw-ginned was steady at 1,825/1,900 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) but F-414 declined by 10 rupees at 2,060/2,080 rupees per maund and Bengal-deshi declined by 10 rupees at 1,030/1,070 rupees per maund.
